title: Planet Earth
description: Earth’s global systems. Plate tectonics, earthquakes, and volcanoes; evolution of our planet and life through geologic time; economic resources including fossil fuels and precious minerals; agents of erosion that shape the land.

title: Dynamics of the Earth Laboratory
description: Hands-on experience with land forms, rocks, minerals, topographic maps, and aerial photographs. Includes demonstrations and field trips. Designed to accompany and augment

title: Earth Science
description: Earth’s four principal reservoirs and their interconnectedness: solid earth, ocean, atmosphere, and biosphere. How humanity affects and is affected by these reservoirs. Most appropriate for liberal studies majors.

title: Earth System History
description: Evolutionary history of earth as traced through rock and fossil records. Stratigraphic and depositional concepts.

title: GIS and Remote Sensing in the Earth and Environmental Sciences
description: Applications of GIS and remote sensing technology. Includes data collection and sources, data storage and organization, data visualization and mapmaking, basic spatial analysis, and ethics and decision-making.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Data Analysis in the Earth and Environmental Sciences I
description: Theory and techniques of geological data analysis. Elementary programming to model statistical processes. Statistical inference, error propagation, plotting, and curve fitting using examples in the earth and environmental sciences.

title: Geology of National Parks and Monuments
description: Geology of a group of national parks and monuments, selected for their geological significance, scenic beauty, and visitor popularity.

title: Data Analysis in the Earth and Environmental Sciences II
description: Builds on GEOL 300 to quantify and explain real-world Earth system datasets. To include advanced data collection, cleaning, analysis, and interpretation. Provides practical experience with leading data analysis tools and software (i.e., Python).

title: Natural Disasters
description: Geologic processes that have dramatically affected the human race: earthquakes, volcanoes, landslides, and floods.

title: Water and the Environment
description: Movement of fresh water on earth. Hydrologic cycling of water from precipitation, runoff, infiltration, stream and groundwater flow to the ocean. Problems caused by over-use of water resources, urbanization, and water pollution examined with case studies.

title: Geologic Inquiry and Problem Solving
description: Guided inquiry field and laboratory approach to solution of geologic problems. Written reports and oral presentations. Required weekend field trips.

title: Geochemistry
description: Fundamental principles of low- and high-temperature geochemistry. Origin of the elements; formation of the solar system; differentiation of the earth; weathering at the earth’s surface; chemistry of natural waters. Laboratory methods applied to geological problems.

title: Mineralogy
description: Practice in determination of common minerals; their geologic environment, utilization, and economic significance. Introduction to optical techniques in mineral identification.

title: Petrology
description: Composition, classification, occurrence, and origin of igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks. Identification of rocks in hand specimen; petrographic analysis of rocks in thin section; modeling and interpretation of petrologic data.

title: Sedimentology and Lithostratigraphy
description: Sedimentologic description and interpretation of the textures and structures of sediments and sedimentary rocks. Stratigraphic analysis of stratal succession, age relationships, and correlation on local and global scales.

title: Academic and Professional Development in the Earth and Environmental Sciences I
description: Exploration and discussion on the nature of science, ethics, civics, artificial intelligence, and other topics. Reflection on and planning for academic and professional development as a scientist within the broader and increasingly complex world.
notes: Taken in fall of junior year

title: Structural Geology
description: Integrates structural and introductory field geology. Principles, causes, and mechanisms of rock deformation combined with field study. Graphical, computer, and analytical techniques for working with folds and faults are applied in the field. Field observations are presented in geologic maps, cross sections, and reports.

title: Geophysics
description: Principles and field studies of gravity, magnetic, and seismic techniques applied to structure, dynamics, and shallow environment of the earth. Computer-aided data reduction and interpretation.

title: Processes and Inquiry in the Earth Sciences
description: Investigation of processes of inquiry and rational thinking skills characteristic of the earth sciences.

title: Academic and Professional Development in the Earth and Environmental Sciences II
description: Applications, activities, and reflections designed to promote academic and professional development in the earth and environmental sciences.
notes: Taken in fall of senior year

title: Internship in Earth and Environmental Sciences
description: Internship with approved private companies, nonprofit organizations, and government agencies. Deliverables co-developed among student, external supervisor, and instructor. Internship report and periodic conferences required. Three units required if being used to fulfill degree requirement.

title: Selected Topics in Geology
description: Selected topics in geology and related earth sciences.

title: Research Methods and Communication
description: Development and testing of scientific hypotheses and their effective communication through oral, written, and visual modes. To be taken prior to registration in

title: Senior Thesis
description: Individual research project, written thesis, and oral presentation done under supervision of professor chosen by student.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study in field, library, laboratory, or museum work.

title: Advanced Field Topics
description: Intensive field-based course focused on a specific disciplinary area of the geological sciences.
notes: See Schedule of Classes for specific content.

title: Advanced Field Geology
description: Investigation of individually assigned areas, preparation of geologic maps, geologic sections, and gathering other types of data as appropriate. Students are responsible for cost of food and transportation. Students must safely perform fieldwork under varied weather, terrain, and time conditions.

title: Process Geomorphology
description: Processes shaping and affecting the earth’s surface, and application of resultant land forms in interpretation of geologic structure, stratigraphy, and neotectonics.

title: Basin Analysis and Energy Resources
description: Analysis of sedimentary basins to determine paleogeography, formation, and subsidence over time using applied modelling and data analysis. Implications for hydrocarbon formation, carbon capture and sequestration, and brine extractions.

title: Geochemistry
description: Fundamental principles of low- and high-temperature geochemistry. Origin of the elements; formation of the solar system; differentiation of the earth; weathering at the earth’s surface; chemistry of natural waters. Laboratory methods applied to geological problems.

title: Notable Historic Earthquakes
description: Earthquake magnitude, fault source physics and rupture mechanisms, earthquake location and ground motion estimation, geotechnical aspects, earthquake triggering and geodesy.

title: Engineering Geology
description: Relationships between geologic processes and works of humans. Topics include rock and soil mechanics, ground water flow, slope stability, seismicity, land subsidence, and evaluation of geologic materials with respect to dam sites, tunnel alignments, and building foundations.

title: Hydrogeology
description: Theory of ground water flow. Exploration for and development of the ground water resource. Aquifer tests, water quality, and water resource management. Occurrence of water in alluvial, sedimentary, volcanic, plutonic, and metamorphic terrains.

title: Advanced Hydrogeology
description: Introduction to numerical modeling of subsurface flow and transport. Emphasizes finite difference methods, model conceptualization, calibration, and application using MODFLOW. Students develop skills to design, evaluate, and present groundwater models for research and professional hydrogeologic problems.

title: Earthquake Seismology
description: Theory of seismic wave excitation, propagation, and recording. Methods of seismogram interpretation and analysis. Applications to tectonics and earthquake hazard analysis.

title: Seismic Interpretation and 3D Visualization
description: Computer-based seismic interpretation, mapping, and modeling in both 2D and 3D. Overview of basic seismic processing. Emphasis on industrial applications, both petroleum and shallow geotechnical.

title: Volcanology
description: Magma and magma chamber properties. Eruptive mechanisms, volcano types, and a variety of volcanic phenomena associated with Hawaiian, Strombolian, Plinian, Vulcanian, and hydrovolcanic eruptions. Volcanic phenomena applied to classic and historic eruptions.

title: Advanced Topics in Geology
description: Advanced special topics in the geological sciences.

title: Seminar
description: An intensive study in advanced geology.
notes: Topic to be announced in the Class Schedule.

title: Advanced Basin Analysis and Energy Resources
description: Analysis of sedimentary basins to determine paleogeography, formation, and subsidence over time using applied modelling and data analysis. Implications for hydrocarbon formation, carbon capture and sequestration, and brine extractions. Individual student analyses and presentations on major sedimentary basins.

title: Coastal and Marine Geology
description: Major geologic processes of coastal and marine environments, to include geomorphology, sedimentation, stratigraphy, volcanism, structural geology, and tectonics. Evaluation of scientific literature and analysis of marine geological and geophysical data.

title: Selected Topics in Geophysics
description: Research topics in seismic, gravity, magnetic, electrical, and electromagnetic methods.

title: Quaternary Geology
description: Quaternary climate, geochronometric dating and soil stratigraphy.

title: Advanced Notable Historic Earthquakes
description: Earthquake magnitude, fault source physics and rupture mechanisms, earthquake location and ground motion estimation, geotechnical aspects, earthquake triggering and geodesy. Term project on a selected earthquake including computer-based analysis of source, mechanism, and location.
notes: Not open to students with credit in

title: Neotectonics
description: Observation, interpretation and significance of late Quaternary crustal deformation.

title: Plate Tectonics
description: To include analysis of plate boundaries, the driving forces of plate tectonics, global plate reconstructions and the predictive power of plate tectonics. Examines the geological and geophysical evidence, and the consequences for the dynamics of Earth’s Interior.

title: Advanced Hydrogeology
description: Introduction to numerical modeling of subsurface flow and transport. Emphasizes finite difference methods, model conceptualization, calibration, and application using MODFLOW. Students develop skills to design, evaluate, and present groundwater models for research and professional hydrogeologic problems.

title: Groundwater Geochemistry
description: Processes affecting inorganic solutes in groundwater. Applications to groundwater geochemical evolution, weathering processes, and inorganic contaminant transport.

title: Earthquake Physics I
description: Structure and theology of fault zones as inferred from geological and geophysical observations. Stress state and frictional behavior of faults, stress interaction models, thermal, and hydrological properties of fault zones. Mechanics and energy budget of earthquakes.

title: Earthquake Physics II
description: Theoretical and numerical models of earthquake rupture and wave propagation, with applications to ground motion prediction and seismic hazard estimation. Collective behavior of fault networks, seismicity models, earthquake predictability; application to earthquake forecast models.

title: Research and Technical Writing
description: Research and technical report writing in geological sciences for students in Plan B.

title: Research
description: Supervised research in an area of geological sciences.

title: Thesis
description: Preparation of a thesis for the master’s degree.

title: Thesis Extension
description: Registration required in any semester or term following assignment of RP in Course 799A in which the student expects to use the facilities and resources of the university; also student must be registered in the course when the completed thesis is granted final approval.

title: Comprehensive Examination Extension
description: Registration required of students whose only requirement is completion of the comprehensive examination for the master’s degree. Registration in 799C limited to two semesters.

title: Doctoral Research
description: Independent investigation in general field of the dissertation.

title: Doctoral Special Study
description: Individual study in field of specialization.

title: Doctoral Dissertation
description: Preparation of the dissertation for the doctoral degree. Enrollment is required during the term in which the dissertation is approved.
